subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should cron runs with successful execution but failed post-run delivery become a first-class `warning` status, or should they remain `ok` with delivery failure recorded only in delivery fields?
rationale: Current main and the latest release lack `warning`, while open PRs implement different public semantics; this changes persisted/API/UI behavior and cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Adopt first-class warning
options.body: Rework or land the broad warning-status path after resolving conflicts and proving Gateway, CLI, UI, docs, and external-client compatibility.

options.title: Keep ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Use the narrower candidate semantics where execution remains `ok` and delivery failure is surfaced through `deliveryStatus` and diagnostics, accepting that Control UI will not have the requested yellow status unless it derives one locally.

options.title: Defer the contract change
options.body: Leave the issue open as a product backlog item and close or pause implementation PRs until maintainers are ready to expand cron status semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt first-class warning
recommendation.body: Rework or land the broad warning-status path after resolving conflicts and proving Gateway, CLI, UI, docs, and external-client compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron status/delivery boundary history points to steipete, and the remaining question is a product/API compatibility choice across core and UI surfaces.
